div.l: So estately was he . of his gouernaūnce .
What with his bargeyns . ⁊and his cheuyssaūnce .
For sothe . he was a worthi man with all .
But sothly to seien . I not how men hym call .
A Clerk ther was . of Oxenforde also .
That vn to logyke . longe tyme had go .
As lene was his hors . as is a rake .
And he was not . right fat I vndir take .
But lokid holwe . ⁊and ther to soberly .
Full thredbare . was his oủerest courtepy .
For he had . geten hym no benefice .
Ne was so worldly . for to haue offyce .
For hym was leuyr . haue at his beddisheed .
Twenty bokes . clad in blak ⁊and reed .
Of Aristotill . ⁊and his philosophie .
Than robes riche . fithell or gay sautrie .
But all be that . he was a philosophre .
Yet had he . but litell golde in his cofre .
But all that he myght . of his frendis hente .
On bokis . ⁊and on lernyng . he it spente .
And besily gan . for the soules preie .
Of hem . that hym yaue wherwith to scoleie .
Of studie . toke he most cure ⁊and hede .
Noght oo worde spak he . more than was nede .
And that was saide . in forme ⁊and reuerence .
And schort ⁊and quyk . ⁊and full of high sentence .
Sownyng in morall vertue . was his speche .
And gladly wolde he lerne . ⁊and gladly teche .
A Sergeant of the lawe . war ⁊and wys .
That ofte . had ben t paruys .
That was also . full riche of excellence .
Discrete he was . ⁊and of gret reuerence .
He semed such . hys wordis were so wyse .
Iustice he was . full ofte in assise .
By patent ⁊and pleyn cōmmyssioıı̄un .
For his scyens . ⁊and for his high renoıı̄un .
Of fees ⁊and robes . had he many oon .
So gret a purchasour . was nowher non .
All was fe symple . to hym in effecte .
His purchasyng . myght not ben infecte .
Nowher so besi a man . as he ther nas .
And yet he semyd . besier than he was .
In termes had he caas . ⁊and domes alle .
That fro the tyme . of kyng William were falle .
Ther to he couthe endite . ⁊and make a thyng .
